title: MILO Marathon 2026 Bacolod Leg Review: Racing in the Visayas' Second City
seo_title: MILO Marathon Bacolod Leg 2026 Review | Negros Occ.
meta_description: MILO Marathon 2026 Bacolod Leg review: October 4 -- part of the 50th-anniversary Golden Run series in the Visayas' second most populous city.
dek: Set for 4 October 2026, this Bacolod leg is one of 15 stops on the MILO Marathon's 50th-anniversary Golden Run series, held in Negros Occidental's capital -- the second most populous city in the entire Visayas after Cebu City.
verdict: The Bacolod leg brings the MILO Marathon's Golden Run series to a genuinely major regional city -- capital of Negros Occidental, and with over 600,000 residents, the second most populous city in the entire Visayas after Cebu City. That scale gives Bacolod real capacity to host a large-field regional leg, even without the extreme historical turnout numbers seen at Cebu specifically. Five distances from 1K to 21K keep it broadly accessible, and the leg carries the same 50th-anniversary institutional weight as every other 2026 stop in the series. Registration status wasn't yet confirmed open at the time of this research.

sections.heading: One of 15 Legs in the Golden Run
paragraphs: The Bacolod leg offers 1K, 3K, 5K, 10K and 21.1K distances, part of the MILO Marathon's 50th-anniversary 'Golden Run' series -- 15 regional legs nationwide ahead of the National Finals in Clark City, Pampanga. [1] That anniversary framing gives every 2026 leg, including Bacolod's, more institutional significance than a routine annual stop.

sections.heading: Bacolod: The Visayas' Second City
paragraphs: Bacolod is a highly urbanized city and the capital of Negros Occidental, with 600,783 residents as of the 2020 census -- the most populous city in the Negros Island Region and the second most populous city in the entire Visayas after Cebu City. [2] Covering roughly 160.71 square kilometres, it's a genuinely major regional hub, giving this leg real capacity for a large field without the logistics squeeze of a small provincial town.

sections.heading: Comparable Scale to Other Major Legs
paragraphs: Bacolod's population puts it in a similar tier to Dumaguete and other regional capitals covered elsewhere in this research batch, though with meaningfully more residents than most -- a genuine mid-sized city with established infrastructure (SM City Bacolod, Bacolod City College, and other landmarks) to support race-day logistics. [2]

paragraphs: As of this writing, registration status for the Bacolod leg has not been confirmed open. [1] Given the city's scale, demand could be significant once registration opens -- worth checking the official MILO site directly rather than waiting for a general announcement.
